history.sg_progress: The initial part of the implementation of the service-level agreement between the Office of Information and Communications Technology and the Office of Administration of Justice has already started. As part of the initial package, the development of an automated synchronization mechanism between the Court Case Management System and the jurisprudence database (Caselaw portal) is under way. The technical teams of the Office of Information and Communications Technology and the Office of Administration of Justice are collaborating in the building of a programming interface that serves to push and receive data between the two systems. In addition, the current Caselaw portal search engine is being enhanced with the ability to use operators such as “add”, “or”, “not”, “must” and “within”. The initial package, including the above components, is undergoing an extensive quality assurance process to make sure that it meets business requirements.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration continue to integrate duplicative system functionalities and data into the further development of new systems under the newly signed service-level agreement with the Office of Information and Communications Technology, thereby enhancing management efficiency and quality.
history.administration_response: In accordance with the established service- level agreement, the teams of both the Office of Information and Communications Technology and the Office of Administration of Justice are proactively working on addressing the Board’s recommendations. An application programming interface to introduce automatic synchronization between the court case management system application and the case law portal is in its final stage of development. The actual judgments and orders (in the form of PDF files) are included as part of the data push between the two systems. The Office of Administration of Justice is performing full validation of the replication mechanism to ensure an accurate representation of all metadata fields in the targeted system (jurisprudence database). Additional labels, fields and categories for orders have been made available in both the court case management system and the case law portal, in which the registries are planning to publish the digests of selected orders. The current case law portal search engine was also enhanced to support the use of operators, and development efforts focused on introducing an additional functionality to enable users to search the content of uploaded documents, including PDF documents, and the digests of judgments and orders.
history.board_assessment: Given that the teams of the Office of Information and Communications Technology and the Office of Administration of Justice are proactively working on addressing the Board’s recommendations, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The Office of Administration of Justice and the Office of Information and Communications Technology continue to collaborate closely on the implementation of this recommendation. Since the last update to the Board, several key milestones have been achieved, including: (a) the development of advanced search functionality, allowing users to perform exact phrase searches, grouped and complex queries, proximity searches and use of operators; (b) digests of selected orders have been published on the Caselaw portal, and (c) the search engine now retrieves results from both the digests and full PDF versions of judgments and orders, with search keywords clearly highlighted. In addition, automatic synchronization between the case and content management system and the Caselaw portal has been successfully implemented for English-language digests. Work is ongoing to identify the most effective solution for automating synchronization of the French-language summaries.
